title: Шеф идёт на поклон к Елене  (The Chef Swallows His Pride with Elena)

segments.t: After ordering his cooks to start prepping immediately, Viktor Petrovich hurries over to Arcobaleno to find Elena Pavlovna. Swallowing his pride, he apologizes for his foolish remarks about male principles and admits that he urgently needs her help to save the wedding banquet.
Живо за работу.
Лен, Лена.
Про работу.
Это ж не про нас.
Это я так, для примера.
Что был неправ.
Но сейчас мне нужна твоя помощь.
Как же твои мужские принципы?
Ты же никогда не хотел зависеть от женщин.
Лен, я не хочу сейчас выяснять отношения.
А я тоже не собиралась выяснять отношения.
Мне в голову не могло прийти.
Кто знал.
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
Живо за работу.
'Get to work, lively now!' Barinov presents a sharp position toward Elena, linking "zhivo" ("quickly, now"), "rabotu" ("job"), and "za" ("for") in one brisk exchange.
Лен, Лена.
'Lena, wait, Lena.' Barinov holds a candid tempo in front of Elena, putting "len" ("Lena") alongside "lena" ("Lena") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
Про работу.
'I was talking about work.' Barinov conveys a measured note across the room, pairing "rabotu" ("job") with "pro" ("about") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
Это ж не про нас.
'That was not about the two of us.' Elena sets a sharp position in the room, pairing "eto" ("this") with "zh" ("after all, but") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
Это я так, для примера.
'I only said that as an example.' Barinov shares a grounded mood in the scene, leaning on "primera" ("example") before closing the thought with "eto" ("this").
Что был неправ.
'To admit that I was wrong.' Elena projects a sharp direction without hesitation, linking "byl" ("was"), "neprav" ("wrong"), and "chto" ("what") in one brisk exchange.
Но сейчас мне нужна твоя помощь.
'And right now I really need your help.' Barinov sets an emphatic view in front of Elena, pairing "seychas" ("now") with "nuzhna" ("needed") so the "-sya" ending carries the action.
Как же твои мужские принципы?
'What happened to your famous male principles?' Elena challenges warmly across the room, weaving "kak" ("how") together with "muzhskiye" ("men's") just the way native speakers do.
Ты же никогда не хотел зависеть от женщин.
'You never wanted to depend on women, remember?' Barinov questions plainly as the beat lands, joining "nikogda" ("never") to "khotel" ("wanted") so every word pulls its weight.
Лен, я не хочу сейчас выяснять отношения.
'Lena, I do not want to argue about our relationship right now.' Barinov projects a clear approach at this moment, joining "len" ("Lena") to "khochu" ("want") so every word pulls its weight.
А я тоже не собиралась выяснять отношения.

'I was not planning to argue about our relationship either.' Barinov strikes a resolute stance in this beat, weaving "tozhe" ("too") together with "sobiralas" ("to intend") just the way native speakers do.
Мне в голову не могло прийти.
'It never would have crossed my mind.' Elena projects a lively stance in the conversation, joining "golovu" ("head") to "moglo" ("can, to be able") so every word pulls its weight.
Кто знал.
'Who could have known?' Barinov questions lightly from the start, pairing "znal" ("knew") with "kto" ("who") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
Живо за работу.
Лен, Лена.
Про работу.
Это ж не про нас.
Это я так, для примера.
Что был неправ.
Но сейчас мне нужна твоя помощь.
Как же твои мужские принципы?
Ты же никогда не хотел зависеть от женщин.
Лен, я не хочу сейчас выяснять отношения.
А я тоже не собиралась выяснять отношения.
Мне в голову не могло прийти.
Кто знал.
That wraps up this scene as desperate for foie gras and extra hands to save the wedding banquet, Chef Barinov goes to Elena Pavlovna to admit he was wrong and ask for her help. See you next time!
До свидания!
